findings.title: Workflow-spawned agents cannot satisfy touch-orchestrate's spawn discipline: no taskId (TaskList empty during a live 5-agent workflow), no description, so no ledger and no TaskStop for exactly the loops README says must be stoppable
Control loop cannot poll while the session is blocked inside a Workflow/agent call; with G6's 120s expiry every stop request is reported expired
control.jsonl is declared single-writer by D5 but the skill makes the session append acks to it; LLM 'append' via Write/Edit can truncate concurrently written intents
The .touch/ -> <task-dir> control-file fallback is ambiguous (relative to what, resolved when) and can permanently split-brain the stop channel
Spawn ledger lives under .claude/local-orchestrators/ which D5 forbids for Touch state, and is undiscoverable by the aggregator; line shape lacks root/cwd/sessionId
Marker precedence conflict: [monitor] is last-wins (watcher:340-345), [touch] is first-line, and plan T8's anchored ^\[monitor\] parse breaks the moment the mandated [touch] line is prepended
No workflow template emits [touch]/names/ledger and neither SKILL.md references touch-orchestrate, so every conforming skill run is non-conforming (proved by this repo's own live orch-scripts)
Touch names and [monitor] plan/stage ids are two unmapped identity systems; per-parent counter N is non-deterministic under parallel(), so names differ across re-runs
A stopped agent is indistinguishable from a crash: filter(Boolean) silently synthesizes from a partial fan-out; implement loop labels a stopped gate 'gate agent died' and burns an attempt
Background Agent-tool spawns write no Workflow journal, so touch-orchestrate's mandated spawn mechanism disables the deterministic decision_watcher both orchestration skills mandate
Background spawns lose schema-validated agent() returns (impl.done / gate.passed / crit.approved), converting the deterministic gated loops into model-mediated ones
Ack vocabulary stopped|not_found|already_done has no mapping into P7's requested/sent/confirmed/expired machine; not_found silently becomes 'expired'
Skill flatly denies pause while README requires it and plan T15 ships a verified hook gate; scope the denial to the spawn/control channel
<task-dir> is undefined for the ad-hoc spawns the skill claims to cover, so state/ledger paths are unresolvable and the model will invent one
description->name parse rule unspecified (em-dash separator, free text); needs a normative regex or names get guessed and poison the (name,attempt)->agentId join
Attempt authority split: research template hardcodes attempt=1, so a re-spawn creates a second agentId for (name,1) and breaks the skill's (name,attempt) uniqueness invariant
Watcher comment claims the marker is appended at the end of the prompt while both templates put it first; misleading for Touch's own parser author

result.summary: Read all four SKILL.md files, both normative *.workflow.js templates, this run's adapted orch-script, and the watcher's marker path, then cross-checked against D1-D14 and the v0 P1-P12 plan. The four skills do NOT compose today. Central contradiction (SKILLS-1, blocker): touch-orchestrate mandates background Agent-tool spawns + a taskId spawn ledger + TaskStop for every spawn, but execute-research/implement-plan spawn exclusively through Workflow agent() — verified empirically that Workflow-spawned agents are not harness tasks (TaskList returned "No tasks found" while five workflow research agents ran), have stub .meta.json with no description, and therefore have no taskId, no ledger line, and no stop path — for exactly the loops README says must be stoppable. Second blocker (SKILLS-2): the control loop cannot poll while the session is blocked inside the Workflow call, and G6's 120s expiry turns every stop request into a false "expired"; the hook gate (T10/T15) is the only channel that reaches a blocked session and should move into v0. Majors: control.jsonl is single-writer per D5 but multi-writer per the skill, with an LLM-Write truncation hazard (SKILLS-3); the .touch/ vs <task-dir> fallback can permanently split-brain the stop channel (SKILLS-4); the spawn ledger sits where D5 forbids Touch state and is undiscoverable (SKILLS-5); marker precedence is unspecified and plan T8's anchored ^\[monitor\] parse breaks as soon as the mandated [touch] line 1 exists, while the watcher is deliberately last-wins (SKILLS-6); no template emits [touch]/names/ledger and neither orchestration skill references touch-orchestrate, so every conforming run is non-conforming — proved by this repo's own live orch-script (SKILLS-7); touch names and [monitor] plan/stage are unmapped identity systems with non-deterministic N under parallel() (SKILLS-8); a stopped agent is indistinguishable from a crash and silently degrades a research barrier (SKILLS-9); background spawns would also kill both the journal-based deterministic watcher (SKILLS-15) and the schema-validated agent() returns the gated loops branch on (SKILLS-16). Minors cover the ack vocabulary mapping, the pause prose contradiction with README/T15, undefined <task-dir> for ad-hoc spawns, the description parse grammar, and split attempt-number authority. Recommendation carried into the file: a two-profile spawn standard (Workflow profile = marker identity, stop declared unavailable; Agent-tool profile = ledger + TaskStop), one canonical .touch/ path set, one marker specification with a fixture test, Touch-native templates with a static guard, and control-record-beats-inference stop/crash disambiguation.

result.summary:
Product-intent / doc-truth pass over README.md, CLAUDE.md, inception.md, .gitignore and the live repo state. Verified empirically: all four monitoring test suites pass (exit 0); git is on `master` with zero commits; ~/.claude/sessions/622.json `procStart` 10028 matches /proc/622/stat field 22 and the registry was measured 214.9 s stale while `status:"busy"` (confirms inception's non-heartbeat claim); monitor_server is live on 8931 (/health ok); both orch-config.json wf_dir paths exist; touch-aggregator/events.jsonl parsed (590 events).

Verdict: the plan (touch-aggregator-plan.md) and inception.md §§1-6 are broadly accurate about the substrate and all their cross-file pointers resolve; CLAUDE.md is the stale artifact and README.md promises a verb the research proved impossible.

Four blockers/decisions the synthesizer must resolve rather than inherit: (1) README:6 demands "pause", which inception §4 and touch-orchestrate both say cannot exist — needs an explicit intent-reconciliation table plus a README edit; (2) CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded and never mentions the normative plan, inception.md, m-orchestrator or touch-orchestrate, so a fresh session re-derives architecture and silently violates D1/D4/D5/D8 — needs an early "read this first" + precedence (plan > inception > CLAUDE.md > README) item; (3) touch-orchestrate's TaskStop/spawn-ledger stop path only works for background Agent-tool spawns, while every execute-research/implement-plan loop is a Workflow agent() spawn with no taskId — so the Stop button is a no-op on the exact loops the product is about; (4) "restart" has two incompatible definitions (D7 Workflow resume vs skill's stop + fresh attempt+1).

Highest-value factual corrections: inception:235 calls the research run complete while the sole machine record reports `failed` — root cause decision_watcher.py:646 closes any plan without a gate verdict as failed, so every execute-research run in this repo is permanently recorded red (no workflow script anywhere emits `orchestrator complete done`); .gitignore has no `.touch/` entry in a zero-commit repo where the first `git add -A` would commit unredacted transcript state; CLAUDE.md:112-114 tells readers to bind 0.0.0.0 on the already-occupied 8931 with no token or Origin allowlist (Touch is 8932); and CLAUDE.md:127-130 + inception:54-56 both tell the reader to discount the task folders as carried-over `omnigent` history when both configs in fact point at this repo's own verified-present wf_dirs.

Also empirically grounded: decision_watcher.py:636-638 labels agents `{role} #{attempt}`, and six distinct agentIds (a2ec1069, a2fc883c, a74f0c93, a79fa2f4, a82d2e25, a9eabf26) all rendered as "research #1" — per-perspective identity survived only in the "best-effort" status.sh stream. That is the concrete justification for making the `[touch] name=` marker mandatory and keying graph nodes on `name`, never on role#attempt.

Binding constraints re-verified for the plan: Touch takes 8932 (8931 occupied); 0.0.0.0 only with per-boot token + Origin/Host allowlist; `.touch/` gitignored before anything creates it; never write under ~/.claude/; never delete a finished task folder; .gitignore edits additive only (test_shell.py:155-161 guards two lines); stdlib-only runtime.
